title: Implement Deep Clone
description:
Implement `deepClone(value)`, which returns a deep copy of `value`.

- Primitives (numbers, strings, booleans, `null`, `undefined`, symbols, bigints) and functions are returned as they are.
- Arrays and plain objects are copied recursively; changing the copy must never change the original. Copies of plain objects keep `Object.prototype` as their prototype, and properties whose value is `undefined` are kept.
- `Date` becomes a new `Date` with the same time. `Map` and `Set` become a new `Map` or `Set` whose keys and values are deep-cloned.
- **Shared and circular references are preserved:** if the same object appears twice in the input, the two places in the copy refer to one cloned object, and an object that contains itself is copied without infinite recursion.

Only own enumerable string keys need copying. You may not use `structuredClone`.

**Constraints:** at most `10^5` values in total; nesting depth at most `1000`.

### How the tests work

Each test is a short script that calls your function and returns what it observed.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Changing the copy leaves the original untouched.
A circular reference in the copy points at the copy itself.

testCases.explanation: Changing the copy leaves the original untouched.
A circular reference in the copy points at the copy itself.

inputs: return [deepClone(5), deepClone('text'), deepClone(null), deepClone(true), deepClone(undefined) === undefined];

const copy = deepClone({ a: undefined, b: null, c: 0 });
return ['a' in copy, copy.a === undefined, copy.b, copy.c, Object.getPrototypeOf(copy) === Object.prototype];
